answer: A registry can require each agent to stake a small deposit and publish a signed history that peers mirror, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes expensive instead of free. A newcomer earns trust only after its juniper-rooted identity, a key tied to a long-lived verifiable record, survives repeated challenges, while a quill-signed audit trail lets anyone check its past work. Sybils can still appear, but each one now costs money and time, and one exposed forgery burns the whole cluster's stake.
